question: The selling price of 20 books is equal to the cost price of 24 books. Find the loss or gain percentage on these books.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given: 20 × SP = 24 × CP ⇒ SP / CP = 24 / 20 = 6 / 5

Profit = SP − CP = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

Gain % = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 20 books = Cost price of 24 books

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

 Profit Calculation using Unitary Method
 
 
 CP of 20 books = ₹20
 
 
 SP of 20 books = ₹24
 
 
 
• 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Profit (₹4)

**Calculations:**

Let the cost price of 1 book be ₹1.

⇒ Cost price of 20 books = 20 × 1 = ₹20

⇒ Selling price of 20 books = Cost price of 24 books = 24 × 1 = ₹24

⇒ Since Selling Price > Cost Price, a profit is made.

⇒ Profit earned on selling 20 books = SP − CP = 24 − 20 = ₹4

⇒ Gain % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (4 ÷ 20) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % is always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer uses a false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ True Value − Error) × 100.
